70826-young-peggy-mcqueen.title: PEGGY McQUEEN
70826-young-peggy-mcqueen.creator: Unknown
70826-young-peggy-mcqueen.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. But Peggy McQueen knew right well what she was about. This was the first day of May, and all around the camp the green grass was bespangled with dew. Is it not a fact, that if a young girl dips her face in the dews of this merry morning, she will be sweet and beautiful all the glad year?

arxiv-1405-2671.title: GEOMETRICAL SCALING AND ITS BREAKING IN HIGH ENERGY COLLISIONS Presented at the 49-th Rencontres de Moriond, March 22-29, 2014, La Thuille, Italy.
arxiv-1405-2671.creator: M. PRASZALOWICZ
arxiv-1405-2671.description: Abstract We report on recent analyses of different pieces of data, which exhibit Geometrical Scaling (GS) and its breaking. GS is a consequence of the existence of an intermediate energy scale, called saturation momentum, and allows to relate data at different energies, of different systems and also at different multiplicities and/or centralities.

arxiv-2101-08334.title: Density-based clustering of social networks
arxiv-2101-08334.creator: Giovanna Menardi, Domenico De Stefano
arxiv-2101-08334.description: Abstract The idea underlying the modal formulation of density-based clustering is to associate groups with the regions around the modes of the probability density function underlying the data. This correspondence between clusters and dense regions in the sample space is here exploited to discuss an extension of this approach to the analysis of social networks.

arxiv-2208-03283.title: Hybrid Gate-Based and Annealing Quantum Computing for Large-Size Ising Problems
arxiv-2208-03283.creator: Chen-Yu Liu, Hsi-Sheng Goan
arxiv-2208-03283.description: Abstract One of the major problems of most quantum computing applications is that the required number of qubits to solve a practical problem is much larger than that of today’s quantum hardware. Therefore, finding a way to make the best of today’s quantum hardware has become a critical issue.

arxiv-2309-09072.title: Parallel Longest Common SubSequence Analysis In Chapel
arxiv-2309-09072.creator: Soroush Vahidi ∗ , Baruch Schieber ∗ , Zhihui Du + , David A. Bader +
arxiv-2309-09072.description: Abstract One of the most critical problems in the field of string algorithms is the longest common subsequence problem (LCS). The problem is NP-hard for an arbitrary number of strings but can be solved in polynomial time for a fixed number of strings.

arxiv-2412-10312.title: Interlocking-free Selective Rationalization Through Genetic-based Learning
arxiv-2412-10312.creator: Federico Ruggeri, Gaetano Signorelli
arxiv-2412-10312.description: Abstract A popular end-to-end architecture for selective rationalization is the select-then-predict pipeline, comprising a generator to extract highlights fed to a predictor. Such a cooperative system suffers from suboptimal equilibrium minima due to the dominance of one of the two modules, a phenomenon known as interlocking .

arxiv-2503-03030.title: On shallow water non-convex dispersive hydrodynamics: the extended KdV model
arxiv-2503-03030.creator: Saleh Baqer, Theodoros P. Horikis, Dimitrios J. Frantzeskakis
arxiv-2503-03030.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate non-classical wavetrain formations, and particularly dispersive shock waves (DSWs), or undular bores, in systems exhibiting non-convex dispersion. Our prototypical model, which arises in shallow water wave theory, is the extended Korteweg-de Vries (eKdV) equation.

arxiv-2601-22135.title: PI-Light: Physics-Inspired Diffusion for Full-Image Relighting
arxiv-2601-22135.creator: Zhexin Liang, Zhaoxi Chen, Yongwei Chen, Tianyi Wei, Tengfei Wang, Xingang Pan
arxiv-2601-22135.description: Abstract Full-image relighting remains a challenging problem due to the difficulty of collecting large-scale structured paired data, the difficulty of maintaining physical plausibility, and the limited generalizability imposed by data-driven priors. Existing attempts to bridge the synthetic-to-real gap for full-scene relighting remain suboptimal.

pmc-10603030.title: Urinary lumirubin excretion in jaundiced preterm neonates during phototherapy with blue light-emitting diode vs. green fluorescent lamp
pmc-10603030.creator: Yumiko Uchida, Yukihiro Takahashi, Chikara Kurata, Yukihiro Morimoto, Eishin Ohtani, Asako Tosaki, Akiko Kumagai, Peter Greimel, Toshiya Nishikubo, Atsushi Miyawaki
pmc-10603030.description: Phototherapy converts lipophilic unconjugated bilirubin to hydrophilic bilirubin photoisomers, such as lumirubin. We comparatively used a blue light-emitting diode (LED) and a green fluorescent lamp (FL) as light sources for phototherapy of hyperbilirubinemic preterm neonates with the aim of examining potential differences in urinary lumirubin excretion between these two wavelengths.

pmc-10731656.title: Protein-Decorated Microbubbles for Ultrasound-Mediated Cell Surface Manipulation
pmc-10731656.creator: Veerle
pmc-10731656.description: Delivering cargo to the cell membranes of specific cell types in the body is a major challenge for a range of treatments, including immunotherapy. This study investigates employing protein-decorated microbubbles (MBs) and ultrasound (US) to “tag” cellular membranes of interest with a specific protein.

pmc-11454235.title: 6450 Leydig Cell Tumor: A Rare Cause of Post-menopausal Hyperandrogenism
pmc-11454235.creator: Rama Nakdali, Shobana Athimulam
pmc-11454235.description: Disclosure: R. Nakdali: None. S. Athimulam: None. Introduction: Ovarian steroid cell tumors are a rare subtype of sex-cord stromal tumors. Leydig cell tumors is a subtype of sex-stromal tumors that is found in < 1% of all ovarian tumors. They are typically benign, unilateral, and secrete androgens which causes virilization.

pmc-11464908.title: Fire performance of CFRP-strengthened piloti-type columns with fire-resistant materials during standard fire exposure
pmc-11464908.creator: Jinwon Shin, Hansol Lee, In-Rak Choi, Jeong-Ki Min, Sung-Mo Choi
pmc-11464908.description: This paper presents a numerical investigation into the fire endurance of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP)-strengthened columns, shielded with fire-resistant materials, in piloti-type reinforced concrete buildings. The strengthened column, equipped with a fire protection system, underwent exposure to the ASTM E119 standard time-temperature curve for a duration of 4 h.

pmc-12641878.title: Knee Taping and the Countermovement Jump: Implications for Reactive Strength, Power, and Jump Mechanics
pmc-12641878.creator: Kendra Taryn Szeles, Andrew Green, Pedro Forte
pmc-12641878.description: Background: The use of knee taping is widely used to enhance stability and landing performance. However, its impact on jumping performance, a key sports performance determinant, remains unknown. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of knee taping on continuous biomechanics during the countermovement jump (CMJ). Methods: Nineteen recreational female netball players (age 22 ± 2.69 years; height 167.

pmc-13068649.title: From animal ethics to climate change: Integrating human-animal-studies and one health into medical education
pmc-13068649.creator: K Widmann, TS Busse, J Ehlers, J Nitsche
pmc-13068649.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The increasing interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health has drawn attention to educational approaches that extend beyond biomedical knowledge and engage with ethical and systemic dimensions of health within the One Health framework.

pmc-13385212.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Antiarrhythmic Drugs on Early Atrial Tachyarrhythmias in the Blanking Period After Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation
pmc-13385212.creator: Asami Kashiwa, Yukio Hosaka, Yuka Hayashi, Komei Tanaka, Kazuyuki Ozaki, Masaomi Chinushi, Yoshifusa Aizawa, Kazuyoshi Takahashi
pmc-13385212.description: BackgroundEarly recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmia (ERAT) after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) is common during the blanking period; however, no standardized management approach exists. This study aimed to identify effective antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) during the blanking period and to examine the association between AAD efficacy and long‐term outcomes.
